chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Mihran ibn Abi Nasr, from his brother Rabah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We are reported in Kufa that Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the completion of Hajj and Umrah is that the man should enter into Ihram from the houses of his family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Has Ali (peace be upon him) said this?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said that for the one whose house is behind the Miqat. And, had it been as they say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have prevented [people] from going out with their clothes to Al-Shajara.'

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الشجرة: Al-Shajara, a specific location in Mecca near the Kaaba
key_terms.مواقيت: Miqat, the designated boundaries or stations for entering Ihram

ai.seo_question: Where should a person living beyond the Miqat enter Ihram for Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of Ihram boundaries by validating the view that those residing beyond the Miqat may enter the state of consecration from their homes, a position attributed to Imam Ali (AS). The Imam reinforces this by citing the Prophet’s practice at Al-Shajara, arguing that if strict adherence to the Miqat line were mandatory for all, the Prophet would not have permitted travelers to don their Ihram garments outside the designated boundary. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical concessions (rukhas) for those living in proximity to or beyond the sacred boundaries, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations found in other schools.
